rationale: Identity was correctly verified via email and the agent used read-only tools to inspect the account and orders. However, the agent changed shipping addresses and the user’s default address without first stating the exact changes and obtaining explicit confirmation, which violates policy. Worse, the agent appears to have selected the wrong address: the user indicated they moved and the luggage set was sent to the new home (592 Elm Ave), but the agent updated both orders and the default address to the profile’s existing address (760 Elm Ave), likely the old address. This contradicts the user’s intent and constitutes an incorrect action. For the tablet, the agent initially attempted an exchange on a pending order (properly blocked by tools), then requested confirmation and successfully modified the pending order to the cheaper option, which was compliant. Despite that, the address-change errors and lack of pre-change confirmation cause the overall outcome to fail the policy bar.
